summary.text: David Hackney is a Democratic member of the Washington House of Representatives for District 11-Position 1, in office since January 11, 2021, and he is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against fellow Democrat Ashley Fedan.
An attorney and former federal prosecutor, he previously served on the Washington State Human Rights Commission.

paragraphs.text: Hackney was born in Cleveland, Ohio.
He earned a bachelor's degree from Cornell University in 1987 and a law degree from Harvard Law School in 1993, and Wikipedia adds a Master of Public Administration from Harvard.

His career includes work as an attorney and federal prosecutor, and Wikipedia reports that he prosecuted for the U.S. Department of Justice in California, taught trial advocacy through the United Nations and later worked in human resources and employee relations at Amazon.
Ballotpedia says he co-founded a community kitchen in Washington, D.C., served on the Washington State Human Rights Commission and served on the board of the Idjwi Island Education Fund.
Hackney won the 2020 Democratic primary against incumbent Zack Hudgins and took office on January 11, 2021.
Ballotpedia lists his 2023-2024 committee assignments as Capital Budget, Consumer Protection & Business and Transportation.
